catalog_quote: 3.3 Tones. Ashe has three level tones, and glide tones that arise from sequences of level tones. The basic conventions are as follows; High ʹ Mid Unmarked Low ˋ Rising ˇ Falling ˆ. The rising and falling tones probably need to be subdivided further. At least some words show contrasts between High-Mid and Mid-Low ... Tones. Tone plays a crucial role in Ashe and it is difficult to see how an effective orthography could ignore this. Numerous plurals are made only by tone. The role of grammatical tone is yet to be explored, but it is unlikely to be minor. ... 5.1.3 Tonally marked plurals. Numerous noun plurals are marked only by tone where the prefix is i-. For monosyllabic stems, the tone on the root remains stable while the low tone singular prefix is raised to Mid or High; ... In polysyllabic words both the prefix and first syllable of the stem, is raised, usually by one level

sources.citation: Jatau, Stephen, Yusuf Tanimu & Muhammad Bello Ubaidallah. 2024. Contrastive Study of Tone and Intonation in Koro Ashe and English: An Implication for Koro Ashe L2 Learners of English. African Journal of Humanities and Contemporary Education Research 14(1): 102-113. DOI 10.62154/e6da6f87 (open access, afropolitanjournals.com). [This is the 'tone and intonation in Koro Ashe' item the second reader could not reach on ResearchGate on 12 Sep.]
sources.quote: 'Koro Ashe is a tonal language and that tone in Koro Ashe is capable of performing both lexical fuction in words like [ìnȧk] L-L 'cow' and [inak] L-H 'sp tree' ... Also, tone in Koro Ashe can perform grammatical function, that is, by changing singular nouns that are spelled the same to plural as it is seen in words; [inak] (L-L) 'cow' and [inak] (H-H) 'cows' ...' (p.112). Tone data are given as L/M/H per syllable (e.g. [inak] 'spp of tree' L-M, p.110), consistent with Blench's three levels. sources.quote: Segmental/phonotactic only: 'Jatau (2012) reveals that Koro Ashe have simple syllable structures that is made up of: v [ai] 'take', v-v [aɛi] 'house', cv [ba] 'come', v-cv [igum] ... and v-cvc [igaɳ]' (p.325). No statement on tone or stress in Koro Ashe. Bibliography identifies Jatau 2012 (MA), Jatau 2021 (Bridge Journal 2(1)) and Jatau 2023 (PhD thesis, NSUK) as further Koro Ashe phonology sources.

sources.note: The only full-length phonology of Koro Ashe known to exist; a contrastive suprasegmental chapter is the one place an explicit statement that Koro Ashe has (or lacks) word stress alongside tone would appear, which would move domain from UNSTATED and could distinguish TONAL from NO-WORD-STRESS. Our record rests on a 30-pp draft sketch silent on stress.
